chunks: [Yahya ibn Muhammad said:] I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'O you who believe! The testimony between you when death approaches one of you, at the time of making the will, shall be two just persons from among you, or two others from among others than you.'

He said: 'Those who are from among you are two Muslims, and those who are from among others than you are from the People of the Book. But if you do not find any from the People of the Book, then from the Magians, because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) established for the Magians the same Sunnah as the People of the Book with regard to the jizyah.'

And that is when a man dies in a foreign land and does not find two Muslims; he should call two men from the People of the Book as witnesses, who shall be detained after the prayer, and they shall both swear by God, Mighty and Majestic: 'We shall not sell it for a price, even if it were a near kinsman, and we shall not conceal God's testimony, for then we would certainly be among the sinners.'

He said: 'And that is when the guardian of the deceased has doubt about their testimony. If it becomes known that the two testified falsely, the guardian is not permitted to invalidate their testimony until he comes with two witnesses who shall stand in place of the first two witnesses, and they shall both swear by God: Our testimony is more rightful than theirs, and we have not transgressed, for then we would certainly be among the wrongdoers.'
So when he does that, the testimony of the first two is invalidated, and the testimony of the later two becomes valid.
God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'This is more appropriate so that they should give testimony in its proper manner, or fear that oaths may be rejected after their oaths.'

key_terms.أهل الكتاب: People of the Book — Jews and Christians who received revealed scriptures
key_terms.الجزية: Jizyah — the poll-tax levied on non-Muslim protected peoples (dhimmis) under Islamic governance
key_terms.المجوس: Magians/Zoroastrians — fire worshippers whom the Prophet treated like People of the Book for legal purposes
key_terms.الوصية: Bequest/Will — the dying person's testamentary declaration
key_terms.الولي: Guardian/Executor — the legal representative of the deceased's estate

ai.seo_question: Who can serve as witnesses for a Muslim's bequest according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains the jurisprudential rulings of Quran 5:106-108 concerning witness requirements for deathbed bequests. He establishes a hierarchy of acceptable witnesses: Muslims first, then People of the Book (Jews and Christians), then Magians (Zoroastrians) based on the Prophet's precedent in extending jizyah to them. He further explains the oath-taking procedure and the mechanism for challenging false testimony, drawing directly on Quranic language as authority.
